=== Overview ===
It is enshrined to the east of the “Haraki Intersection” on {{ill|Japan National Route 136|Q11421406|qid=Q11421406}}.

Although the date of foundation is unknown, as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinai shrine}}, it dates back to before {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), when the ‘{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}’ was compiled<ref>[https://kotobank.jp/word/神名帳-82644 What is the Jinmyōchō?] - {{ill|Kotobank|Q11302260|qid=Q11302260}}</ref>.

In the ‘{{ill|Izu Province Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}’, it is recorded as “Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Araki no Myōjin.”

Before the Edo period, it was also called Ibaraki Shrine (Ibaraki Jinja), and given that there was an old place name Tagata District Ibaraki Township, the shrine/place names “Araki” and “Haraki” are thought to be phonetic corruptions of “Ibaraki”<ref name="sbs"/><ref name="yuisho">On-site shrine history plaque</ref>.

In addition, due to a legend that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} frequently visited the shrine during his time in exile and hung his horse’s saddle on a tree in front of the torii gate, it was also known as Kurakake Shrine (Kurakake Myōjin)<ref name="yuisho"/>.

In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 12 ({{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}}), it was designated a gōsha, and on April 12 of Meiji 40 ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}), it was designated a shrine authorized to receive offerings of sacred food and heihaku.

At the grand festival in October, as with other shrines in the city, the {{ill|Sanbasō|Q11356796|qid=Q11356796}} dance is performed<ref name="sbs"/>.
